title: Fatty Liver Disease Explained: Symptoms, Causes & Can It Be Reversed?

sentences.zh: 这包括六个月的WhatsApp支持、四场小组大师班、大师课、个性化指导、一份福特纳姆和梅森的礼品，以及限时的一对一辅导奖励。

sentences.zh: 报名截止时间为11月16日星期一晚上10点。

sentences.zh: 请通过我在描述中链接的奖励页面了解更多信息。

sentences.zh: 请记住，你必须通过我的链接购买才能获得我的奖励。

sentences.zh: 如果你有任何问题，我随时为你解答。

sentences.en: Most people think liver disease equals alcohol.
sentences.zh: 大多数人认为肝病等于酗酒。

sentences.en: It doesn't.
sentences.zh: 事实并非如此。

sentences.en: Fatty liver disease is rising.
sentences.zh: 脂肪肝疾病的发病率正在上升。

sentences.en: It can be genetic, but not always.
sentences.zh: 它可能是遗传性的，但并非总是如此。

sentences.en: It's often silent.
sentences.zh: 它通常是隐匿的。

sentences.en: But in many cases, if caught early enough, it can be reversible.
sentences.zh: 但在许多情况下，如果发现得足够早，它是可以逆转的。

sentences.en: So why haven't we heard more about it?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么我们对它了解得不多呢？

sentences.en: Today, I'm speaking with Sharon Verma,
sentences.zh: 今天，我采访了莎伦·维尔马，

sentences.en: an NHS health coach whose father died from the disease and who has made it her life's mission to make sure other families don't learn about it too late.
sentences.zh: 她是一位英国国家医疗服务体系（NHS）的健康教练，她的父亲因这种疾病去世，她已将确保其他家庭不会太晚发现这种疾病作为自己的人生使命。

sentences.en: Hope you find it so useful.
sentences.zh: 希望你觉得这很有用。

sentences.en: If you do, please like, comment, share and subscribe for more.
sentences.zh: 如果觉得有用，请点赞、评论、分享并订阅以获取更多内容。

sentences.en: Hi, I just want to welcome along Sharon Verma to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我想欢迎莎伦·维尔马来到播客。

sentences.en: Hi, Sharon.
sentences.zh: 你好，莎伦。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Lovely to have you here and thank you for staying in touch since we met at an in-person event just about six months ago, probably it was, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能来，也谢谢你自从我们大约六个月前在一次线下活动中见面后一直保持联系，大概是六个月前吧，对吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it was about six months ago where we met at the event.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们是在大约六个月前的活动上见面的。

sentences.en: And I love talking with you, but I also love learning and that's why I've invited you on the podcast because you were telling me about something that I have never heard of before.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢和你交谈，我也喜欢学习，这就是我邀请你上播客的原因，因为你告诉了我一些我以前从未听说过的事情。

sentences.en: And I would wager that probably lots of people haven't heard about before and I think it sounds quite important.
sentences.zh: 我敢打赌，很多人可能都没听说过，而且我觉得这听起来相当重要。

sentences.en: So I thought we'd do a little bit of public information.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们应该做一点公共信息普及。

sentences.en: Could you tell us what you are now kind of an expert in?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我们你现在算是哪方面的专家吗？

sentences.en: So I specialize in something called what used to be called non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.
sentences.zh: 我专门研究一种以前被称为非酒精性脂肪肝的疾病。

sentences.en: But the name has now changed to metabolic dysfunction associated steostatic liver disease.
sentences.zh: 但现在名称已更改为代谢功能障碍相关脂肪性肝病。

sentences.en: Now, liver disease affects one in five people in the UK and it's asymptomatic.
sentences.zh: 目前，英国每五个人中就有一人患有肝病，而且它是无症状的。

sentences.en: So you could easily dismiss this.
sentences.zh: 所以你很容易忽视它。

sentences.en: You may feel fatigued.
sentences.zh: 你可能会感到疲劳。

sentences.en: Maybe you have maybe a dull aches, things that you could easily dismiss.
sentences.zh: 也许你会有隐隐作痛的感觉，这些都是你很容易忽视的事情。

sentences.en: And it's not always picked up in the routine blood teSt.
sentences.zh: 而且它并不总能在常规血液检查中被发现。

sentences.en: Yes, sometimes it may be picked up so your ALT levels may be high so your doctor may check that.
sentences.zh: 是的，有时可能会被发现，比如你的谷丙转氨酶（ALT）水平可能偏高，所以医生可能会检查一下。

sentences.en: But more often than not, because our liver is so resilient, it will carry on working away even when it's inflamed.
sentences.zh: 但更多时候，因为我们的肝脏非常有弹性，即使在发炎时它也会继续工作。

sentences.en: And that's when problems start to occur.
sentences.zh: 而这就是问题开始出现的时候。

sentences.en: But it's not spoken about enough.
sentences.zh: 但关于它的讨论还不够多。

sentences.en: No, let's really go back to basics.
sentences.zh: 没错，让我们回归基础。

sentences.en: What are ALT levels and what does our liver do for us?
sentences.zh: 什么是ALT水平，我们的肝脏为我们做了什么？

sentences.en: So an ALT is when your liver is inflamed, it's almost like a stress hormone or protein that gets delivered into the bloodstream.
sentences.zh: ALT是指当你的肝脏发炎时，它就像一种压力激素或蛋白质被释放到血液中。

sentences.en: And when that's elevated, so say, for example, your reading is coming up quite high.
sentences.zh: 当它升高时，比如，你的读数变得相当高。

sentences.en: So say it's gone over 35.
sentences.zh: 比如超过了35。

sentences.en: Your doctor may see it and think, oh, OK, it's a little bit abnormal, but it's fine.
sentences.zh: 你的医生可能会看到它并认为，哦，好吧，有点异常，但没关系。

sentences.en: We'll do another check.
sentences.zh: 我们再做一次检查。

sentences.en: But if it's consistently high, then your doctor should really go and do a ultrasound and see the texture of your liver and see if there are any fatty deposits.
sentences.zh: 但如果它持续偏高，那么你的医生真的应该去做超声波检查，看看你肝脏的质地，看看是否有脂肪沉积。

sentences.en: Because the sooner you catch it, the easier it is to reverse.
sentences.zh: 因为发现得越早，就越容易逆转。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: So in the early stages, it's something that you can reverse.
sentences.zh: 所以在早期阶段，它是可以逆转的。

sentences.en: It is, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对可以。

sentences.en: But if it progresses, then it sounds like the liver gets less plastic, more rigid and scarred.
sentences.zh: 但如果它继续恶化，听起来肝脏会变得不那么有弹性，而是变得更僵硬、更有疤痕。

sentences.en: So the way to look, to think of your liver, it's a nice, soft texture.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以把肝脏想象成一种质地柔软的东西。

sentences.en: When you have a fatty liver, you'll have fatty deposits and the liver will become inflamed.
sentences.zh: 当你患有脂肪肝时，会有脂肪沉积，肝脏会发炎。

sentences.en: If you cannot calm down that inflammation and say, for example, it progresses from a mild fatty liver to moderate and then severe, it will start to scar.
sentences.zh: 如果你不能平息这种炎症，比如，它从轻度脂肪肝发展到中度，再到重度，它就会开始结疤。

sentences.en: And that leads to something called liver fibrosis.
sentences.zh: 这会导致一种叫做肝纤维化的疾病。

sentences.en: Now, liver fibrosis has four stages.
sentences.zh: 肝纤维化有四个阶段。

sentences.en: It's known as F0 to F4.
sentences.zh: 被称为F0到F4。

sentences.en: F0 to F2 is reversible, so you can stop it.
sentences.zh: F0到F2是可以逆转的，所以你可以阻止它。

sentences.en: But when it gets to F3, F4, you cannot stop the scarring in terms of going to liver cirrhosis.
sentences.zh: 但当它发展到F3、F4时，你就无法阻止向肝硬化发展的疤痕形成过程了。

sentences.en: You can stop yourself from getting to cirrhosis, which is end-stage liver disease, but you cannot reverse the scarring at that point.
sentences.zh: 你可以阻止自己发展到肝硬化，也就是终末期肝病，但在那个阶段你无法逆转疤痕。

sentences.en: When you get to liver cirrhosis, the shape of the liver has now changed.
sentences.zh: 当你患上肝硬化时，肝脏的形状已经改变了。

sentences.en: And there are two types.
sentences.zh: 有两种类型。

sentences.en: So you've got a decompensated liver or you'll have a compensated liver.
sentences.zh: 一种是失代偿性肝硬化，另一种是代偿性肝硬化。

sentences.en: If you have liver cirrhosis and your liver is compensated, your body is still functioning as it should.
sentences.zh: 如果你患有肝硬化但肝脏处于代偿期，你的身体仍然可以正常运作。

sentences.en: Our liver is so loyal and so resilient, it will keep working away.
sentences.zh: 我们的肝脏非常忠诚且有弹性，它会一直坚持工作。

sentences.en: If it is decompensated, that's where your liver is struggling and you will know about it.
sentences.zh: 如果是失代偿期，那就是你的肝脏在挣扎，你会察觉到的。

sentences.en: You will have yellowing of the skin and eyes.
sentences.zh: 你会出现皮肤和眼睛发黄。

sentences.en: You will have severe itching.
sentences.zh: 你会感到剧烈瘙痒。

sentences.en: You will have fluid build-up.
sentences.zh: 你会出现积液。

sentences.en: You will maybe hallucinate.
sentences.zh: 你可能会产生幻觉。

sentences.en: You will lose muscle mass.
sentences.zh: 你会流失肌肉量。

sentences.en: And at that point, your stages are quite bleak.
sentences.zh: 在那个阶段，情况相当严峻。

sentences.en: You're either looking at a liver transplant if you're lucky, or sadly, it will end in death.
sentences.zh: 如果你幸运的话，可能需要进行肝移植，或者不幸的话，最终会导致死亡。

sentences.en: So for me, due to my personal experience with it, it's really important, A, to get the word out, and B, to get people talking about their liver.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，由于我的个人经历，A，传播这个信息，B，让人们谈论他们的肝脏，是非常重要的。

sentences.en: Getting people to understand how vital this organ is.
sentences.zh: 让人们了解这个器官有多么重要。

sentences.en: It's just as vital as the heart, and the way to think about your liver is a bit like the head of an orchestra, the conductor.
sentences.zh: 它和心脏一样重要，你可以把肝脏想象成管弦乐队的指挥。

sentences.en: If he's doing his thing properly, everything's going to be in sync.
sentences.zh: 如果他指挥得当，一切都会同步。

sentences.en: The musicians are going to be all playing a nice tune.
sentences.zh: 音乐家们都会演奏出美妙的旋律。

sentences.en: It's the same thing with our organs.
sentences.zh: 我们的器官也是一样。

sentences.en: If the liver's working well, all the organs will function.
sentences.zh: 如果肝脏工作良好，所有器官都会正常运作。

sentences.en: If the liver's struggling, then your other organs will struggle too.
sentences.zh: 如果肝脏在挣扎，那么你的其他器官也会跟着挣扎。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So it's the kind of, it just quietly ticks away and does what it does.
sentences.zh: 所以它就是那种默默地工作，做好自己的本职工作。

sentences.en: It's incredible.
sentences.zh: 这太不可思议了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And as you were speaking, I was thinking, oh, the itching.
sentences.zh: 你刚才说话的时候，我在想，哦，瘙痒。

sentences.en: That reminds me, when I was pregnant, that was something that you really needed to look out for.
sentences.zh: 这让我想起，我怀孕的时候，那是确实需要注意的事情。

sentences.en: Because I think livers can flare up during pregnancy.
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得怀孕期间肝脏可能会发作。

sentences.en: During pregnancy, yeah.
sentences.zh: 怀孕期间，是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And then the cirrhosis, I have heard about, I'd heard about before, but linked to alcohol.
sentences.zh: 关于肝硬化，我以前听说过，但那是和酒精联系在一起的。

sentences.en: And fatty liver disease is something different to that, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 而脂肪肝疾病与此不同，对吧？

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 是的，不同。

sentences.en: Fatty liver disease is a first stage.
sentences.zh: 脂肪肝疾病是第一阶段。

sentences.en: So you have a healthy liver.
sentences.zh: 所以你有一个健康的肝脏。

sentences.en: That liver then turns into a fatty liver that then goes to fibrosis.
sentences.zh: 那个肝脏然后变成脂肪肝，接着发展成纤维化。

sentences.en: And then when it gets a cirrhosis, that's where you could, there's nothing you can do about it then.
sentences.zh: 然后当它变成肝硬化时，那就无能为力了。

sentences.en: Which is why when you're first diagnosed with liver disease, say, for example, you're at the doctor's office and doctors, oh, you've got mild fatty liver disease,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么当你第一次被诊断出患有肝病时，比如，你在医生办公室，医生说，哦，你患有轻度脂肪肝疾病，

sentences.en: go and lose some weight.
sentences.zh: 去减减肥吧。

sentences.en: That is the first advice you will be given.
sentences.zh: 这是你得到的第一个建议。

sentences.en: Go and lose some weight.
sentences.zh: 去减减肥吧。

sentences.en: But it's not helpful.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有什么帮助。

sentences.en: Because you can go onto any kind of diet thinking, I will lose some weight.
sentences.zh: 因为你可以尝试任何一种饮食，认为我会减掉一些体重。

sentences.en: But what research has shown and what the evidence shows is the Mediterranean style approach is the most, you know, the best approach to help somebody reverse fatty liver disease.
sentences.zh: 但研究表明，证据显示地中海式的饮食方法是帮助人们逆转脂肪肝疾病的最佳方法。

sentences.en: OK, so you might think, well, I'll have smaller portions of my chips or smaller portions of my of my curries that might be laced with ghee or whatever,
sentences.zh: 好的，所以你可能会想，好吧，我会少吃点薯条，或者少吃点可能加了酥油的咖喱，或者其他什么，

sentences.en: or smaller portions of my deep fried food.
sentences.zh: 或者少吃点油炸食品。

sentences.en: And that will help me lose weight, which it will, but it won't necessarily impact on your liver.
sentences.zh: 这确实会帮助我减肥，但它不一定会对你的肝脏产生影响。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: And how did you come to have such a professional and personal interest in this, Sharon?
sentences.zh: 莎伦，你是怎么对这个领域产生如此专业和个人兴趣的？

sentences.en: So my dad was diagnosed in early 2001.
sentences.zh: 我父亲在2001年初被诊断出患有此病。

sentences.en: So I would have been about mid-20s.
sentences.zh: 那时我大概20多岁。

sentences.en: And at that point, he had a dull ache on the side of his abdomen.
sentences.zh: 当时，他的腹部一侧有隐隐作痛的感觉。

sentences.en: He ignored it for quite a while until he couldn't ignore it anymore.
sentences.zh: 他忽略了很长一段时间，直到他再也无法忽视为止。

sentences.en: So he went to A&E.
sentences.zh: 所以他去了急诊室。

sentences.en: And there, the doctors thought it was probably his appendix.
sentences.zh: 在那里，医生认为可能是阑尾炎。

sentences.en: But when they checked further, they found out he's actually got liver disease.
sentences.zh: 但当他们进一步检查时，发现他实际上患有肝病。

sentences.en: So he had a fatty liver.
sentences.zh: 他患有脂肪肝。

sentences.en: And when they told him he'd got liver disease, his response was, liver disease, I don't drink alcohol.
sentences.zh: 当他们告诉他患有肝病时，他的反应是，肝病？我不喝酒。

sentences.en: And they said, look, go and see your doctor.
sentences.zh: 他们说，去看看你的医生。

sentences.en: Your doctor will explain it.
sentences.zh: 你的医生会解释的。

sentences.en: So the doctor said to him, yes, you've got liver disease.
sentences.zh: 医生告诉他，是的，你患有肝病。

sentences.en: Go and lose some weight.
sentences.zh: 去减减肥吧。

sentences.en: And they gave him a booklet.
sentences.zh: 他们给了他一本小册子。

sentences.en: But no one even thought to ask, can this man read?
sentences.zh: 但没有人想到要问，这个人识字吗？

sentences.en: He couldn't.
sentences.zh: 他不识字。

sentences.en: He couldn't read or write English.
sentences.zh: 他不会读写英语。

sentences.en: And so when he told us, I've got liver disease, we dismissed it.
sentences.zh: 所以当他告诉我们他患有肝病时，我们不相信。

sentences.en: We said, Dad, there's no way you've got liver disease.
sentences.zh: 我们说，爸爸，你不可能患有肝病。

sentences.en: You don't drink alcohol.
sentences.zh: 你不喝酒。

sentences.en: This liver disease only happens to people who can't handle their drink.
sentences.zh: 这种肝病只会发生在那些酗酒的人身上。

sentences.en: You don't even drink.
sentences.zh: 你甚至都不喝酒。

sentences.en: But it was only after I spoke to the doctor that I understood this is actually down to his diet, his diet and his lifestyle.
sentences.zh: 但直到我和医生谈过之后，我才明白这实际上是由于他的饮食，他的饮食和生活方式造成的。

sentences.en: And he has to lose some weight.
sentences.zh: 他必须减掉一些体重。

sentences.en: And so Dad's method of weight loss was, I will have an apple for breakfaSt.
sentences.zh: 所以爸爸的减肥方法是，早餐吃一个苹果。

sentences.en: I will go on long walks.
sentences.zh: 去长距离散步。

sentences.en: I'll have my main, like, chapati and curry in the evening.
sentences.zh: 晚上吃主食，比如印度薄饼和咖喱。

sentences.en: And then that will work.
sentences.zh: 然后这样就会有效。

sentences.en: And yeah, he lost weight.
sentences.zh: 是的，他确实瘦了。

sentences.en: But he lost muscle mass.
sentences.zh: 但他流失的是肌肉量。

sentences.en: He didn't lose the fat that he needed to lose.
sentences.zh: 他没有减掉他需要减掉的脂肪。

sentences.en: So by the time a year later he goes to get his liver scanned, he's then told, your liver's now progressed to liver fibrosis.
sentences.zh: 所以一年后当他去扫描肝脏时，他被告知，你的肝脏现在已经发展为肝纤维化了。

sentences.en: Again, go lose some weight.
sentences.zh: 还是那句话，去减减肥吧。

sentences.en: There wasn't any thorough checking being done or monitoring being done until he got to liver cirrhosis.
sentences.zh: 在他发展到肝硬化之前，没有任何彻底的检查或监测。

sentences.en: Now, when he got to liver cirrhosis, he was told, oh, don't worry, you know, you probably need about two, three years until you need a transplant.
sentences.zh: 当时他被诊断出肝硬化时，医生告诉他，别担心，你可能还需要两三年才需要做移植手术。

sentences.en: That wasn't the case for him.
sentences.zh: 但对他来说情况并非如此。

sentences.en: His liver started to deteriorate very quickly.
sentences.zh: 他的肝脏开始迅速恶化。

sentences.en: So his liver became decompensated.
sentences.zh: 他的肝脏出现了失代偿。

sentences.en: So Dad had ascetes, which is fluid buildup in his abdomen.
sentences.zh: 我爸爸出现了腹水，也就是腹部积液。

sentences.en: But he would resemble, say, a pregnant woman.
sentences.zh: 看起来就像个孕妇一样。

sentences.en: It would be that much.
sentences.zh: 积液量非常多。

sentences.en: And he would have to go to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 他不得不去医院。

sentences.en: He'd be admitted and a doctor would have to insert a needle about that big into his abdomen.
sentences.zh: 他会被收治入院，医生必须把一根那么粗的针扎进他的腹部。

sentences.en: He'd lay still for about eight to nine hours for the fluid to be drained.
sentences.zh: 他得静卧八到九个小时，让积液排出来。

sentences.en: And at first this was being done monthly.
sentences.zh: 起初是一个月一次。

sentences.en: It then went to biweekly.
sentences.zh: 后来变成两周一次。

sentences.en: It then went to weekly.
sentences.zh: 再后来变成一周一次。

sentences.en: And then it was every other day.
sentences.zh: 最后变成了隔天一次。

sentences.en: And my brother and I, you know, we could see he's in trouble here.
sentences.zh: 我和我哥哥都能看出他情况不妙。

sentences.en: So we were calling King's College Hospital every single day because they are the most renowned hospital for liver disease patients.
sentences.zh: 所以我们每天都给国王学院医院打电话，因为那是治疗肝病最著名的医院。

sentences.en: We didn't know when Dad was diagnosed, but by the time, you know, it came to Dad nearing his end, we then found out where he should have been.
sentences.zh: 爸爸刚确诊时我们并不了解，但等到他快不行的时候，我们才发现他本该去哪家医院治疗。

sentences.en: And when he finally did get to King's Hospital, we were like, oh, just take our liver.
sentences.zh: 当他终于住进国王学院医院时，我们当时就说，求求你们，用我们的肝吧。

sentences.en: And the doctor was like, that's not how it works.
sentences.zh: 医生却说，移植不是这么运作的。

sentences.en: One, we need to make sure that your dad's liver is at a point where we can offer him a transplant.
sentences.zh: 第一，我们需要确保你爸爸的肝脏状况达到了可以接受移植的程度。

sentences.en: Two, we need to make sure if you're healthy enough to have, you know, to give your liver to your dad.
sentences.zh: 第二，我们需要确保你的身体足够健康，能够把肝脏捐给你爸爸。

sentences.en: And, you know, there's so much more to it.
sentences.zh: 而且，这远比这复杂得多。

sentences.en: We can't just open you up and give half your liver.
sentences.zh: 我们不能直接把你剖开，切走一半肝脏。

sentences.en: And then, sadly, Dad slipped into a coma because his liver started to release toxins into his body.
sentences.zh: 后来，不幸的是，爸爸陷入了昏迷，因为他的肝脏开始向体内释放毒素。

sentences.en: And then eight weeks after he turned 60, he passed away.
sentences.zh: 在他60岁生日八周后，他去世了。

sentences.en: I'm so sorry to hear that.
sentences.zh: 听到这个消息我很难过。

sentences.en: And that is so young.
sentences.zh: 而且他太年轻了。

sentences.en: You know, I lost my dad at 71, and I consider that young.
sentences.zh: 我父亲去世时71岁，我都觉得他走得太早了。

sentences.en: But, you know, for you to lose your dad when you were a young woman, I think before you had children as well.
sentences.zh: 而你父亲去世时你还那么年轻，我想那时你甚至还没生孩子。

sentences.en: Yeah, right, before I got married, it's really bitter.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错，那时我还没结婚，这真的很苦涩。

sentences.en: It's bittersweet because I've got this, you can almost call it a black cloud over my head, thinking I'm now helping people, reverse fatty liver disease,
sentences.zh: 这是一种苦乐参半的感觉，因为我心里总像压着一片乌云，想着我现在在帮助人们逆转脂肪肝疾病，

sentences.en: but I wasn't able to save him.
sentences.zh: 但我却没能救下他。

sentences.en: And it's a guilt that I know I shouldn't have, but I do have.
sentences.zh: 我知道我不该有这种负罪感，但我确实有。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全理解。

sentences.en: We can only do what we do with the knowledge we've got at the time, right?
sentences.zh: 我们只能在当时已知的知识范围内尽力而为，对吧？

sentences.en: And this is why this kind of public information is so important, because actually people will learn about livers, will perhaps learn about this fatty liver name,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么这种公共信息如此重要，因为人们会去了解肝脏，或许会了解到“脂肪肝”这个名称，

sentences.en: although they've changed that now.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们现在已经改名了。

sentences.en: Could you remind us the new name and get really slowly for us so that we can really hear the words.
sentences.zh: 你能提醒我们一下新名称吗？请说慢一点，让我们能听清每一个词。

sentences.en: Abbreviation is known as MAZLD, but the actual wording is metabolic dysfunction associated steostatic liver disease.
sentences.zh: 缩写是MAZLD，全称是代谢功能障碍相关脂肪性肝病。

sentences.en: Okay, but you might still hear it called fatty liver disease.
sentences.zh: 好的，但你可能还是会听到人们叫它脂肪肝疾病。

sentences.en: Your doctor may call it NAFLD, which is non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.
sentences.zh: 你的医生可能会称之为NAFLD，即非酒精性脂肪性肝病。

sentences.en: NAFLD.
sentences.zh: NAFLD。

sentences.en: N-A-F-L-D.
sentences.zh: N-A-F-L-D.

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Which is what it used to be called, but now they've changed it to MAZLD.
sentences.zh: 这曾是它的旧称，但现在他们改成了MAZLD。

sentences.en: Oh, and it feels like it should have been a simpler name, but I feel like they've made it more complicated.
sentences.zh: 哦，感觉应该有个更简单的名字，但我觉得他们把它搞得更复杂了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: But there is a reason why they've done that, and I understand why they've done that, because there's a real stigma around liver disease.
sentences.zh: 但他们这么做是有原因的，我理解他们的初衷，因为肝病确实存在严重的污名化。

sentences.en: You tell anyone, I've got, you know, I have an issue with my liver.
sentences.zh: 如果你告诉任何人，我有肝脏方面的问题。

sentences.en: First thing people think of is alcohol.
sentences.zh: 人们首先想到的就是酒精。

sentences.en: And I hold my hand up.
sentences.zh: 我得举手承认。

sentences.en: I was one of those people before dad was diagnosed.
sentences.zh: 在爸爸确诊之前，我就是那样的人。

sentences.en: And that's the start of reality of liver disease.
sentences.zh: 这就是肝病现实的开端。

sentences.en: You know, it's not spoken about just this enough.
sentences.zh: 关于这个话题，讨论得还远远不够。

sentences.en: It's got the stigma behind it.
sentences.zh: 它背后背负着污名。

sentences.en: People feel like it's their fault.
sentences.zh: 人们觉得这是他们自己的错。

sentences.en: It's not.
sentences.zh: 其实并不是。

sentences.en: It can happen to anyone.
sentences.zh: 它可能发生在任何人身上。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And yeah, it is the alcohol.
sentences.zh: 而且，确实有酒精引起的肝病。

sentences.en: And it's similar to pancreatitis, right?
sentences.zh: 这和胰腺炎很像，对吧？

sentences.en: Because you think, oh, pancreatitis, that's often alcohol.
sentences.zh: 因为你会想，哦，胰腺炎，那通常是喝酒引起的。

sentences.en: But actually, this is not that.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，肝病并非都是如此。

sentences.en: And, you know, like you said, your dad didn't drink.
sentences.zh: 而且，就像你说的，你爸爸不喝酒。

sentences.en: So it definitely wasn't that.
sentences.zh: 所以肯定不是那个原因。

sentences.en: Do you know, when you look at family history, was anyone in his family struggling with this, even if you maybe didn't realize at the time?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，当你回顾家族史时，他家里有人曾受此困扰吗？哪怕当时你们没意识到？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, funnily enough, I shouldn't say funnily enough, but after dad passed away, we then found out that dad's dad had liver, a fatty liver as well.
sentences.zh: 说来有趣，我不该说有趣，但在爸爸去世后，我们才发现我爷爷也有脂肪肝。

sentences.en: So it's obviously genetics in my family.
sentences.zh: 所以这显然是我们家族的遗传问题。

sentences.en: But we never, I didn't, I never knew my granddad had a fatty liver.
sentences.zh: 但我以前从不知道我爷爷有脂肪肝。

sentences.en: You know, had we have known granddad had that, then maybe we would have been more aware of it from, you know, when my dad was diagnosed, but we weren't aware.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果我们早知道爷爷有这个病，也许在爸爸确诊时我们会有更多防范意识，但当时我们并不知情。

sentences.en: And is it only with hindsight that they were like, oh, yeah, he always was a bit yellow and he did always have sort of yellow whites of his eyes?
sentences.zh: 是不是只有事后回想起来，才会觉得“哦，对，他总是有点发黄，眼白也总是黄黄的”？

sentences.en: Or did he always, was he already getting treatment for his liver when he was alive?
sentences.zh: 还是说他在世时就已经在接受肝病治疗了？

sentences.en: He used to live in Nairobi, Kenya, and apparently he was getting treated there, but he never told his children or his grandchildren.
sentences.zh: 他以前住在肯尼亚的内罗毕，据说他在那里接受过治疗，但他从未告诉过他的子女或孙辈。

sentences.en: It was something he kept to himself.
sentences.zh: 这是他一直藏在心里的事。

sentences.en: But had they have actually just explained what was happening with him, it would have educated the whole family.
sentences.zh: 但如果他们当时能把他的病情解释清楚，那就能教育整个家族了。

sentences.en: And that's what's lacking.
sentences.zh: 而这正是目前所缺失的。

sentences.en: Even now, the education isn't there.
sentences.zh: 即使是现在，相关的教育依然匮乏。

sentences.en: Even now, like, you know, I've been part of the NHS for about three years now.
sentences.zh: 即使现在，我在国民医疗服务体系（NHS）工作也快三年了。

sentences.en: And I've seen firsthand how liver patients are being let down.
sentences.zh: 我亲眼目睹了肝病患者是如何被忽视的。

sentences.en: I've seen how liver patients are told, oh, yeah, just go lose some weight.
sentences.zh: 我看到肝病患者被告知，“哦，去减减肥吧”。

sentences.en: But there's no help behind it.
sentences.zh: 但后面没有任何后续帮助。

sentences.en: You know, there's no follow up.
sentences.zh: 没有后续跟进。

sentences.en: There's no, OK, you know what, come back in six months, let's read your blood, let's go and make sure you're getting your scans done.
sentences.zh: 没有那种“好吧，六个月后再来复查，我们要看你的血液指标，确保你做了扫描检查”的流程。

sentences.en: There have been times where a case has been sent to me saying, this is a fatty liver patient, please help them.
sentences.zh: 有时会有病例转给我，说这是个脂肪肝患者，请帮帮他们。

sentences.en: So when I've called them, I've seen, oh, yeah, your doctor sent through the referral.
sentences.zh: 当我给他们打电话时，我发现他们会说，“哦，是医生发来的转诊吗？”

sentences.en: I can see you've been diagnosed with fatty liver disease.
sentences.zh: “我看到你被诊断出患有脂肪肝。”

sentences.en: And the patient is, I haven't got a fatty liver.
sentences.zh: 而患者会说，“我没有脂肪肝啊。”

sentences.en: What are you talking about?
sentences.zh: “你在说什么？”

sentences.en: No one's told me.
sentences.zh: “没人告诉过我。”

sentences.en: And that is, the change has to start.
sentences.zh: 这就是现状，必须做出改变。

sentences.en: We need to see change within the NHS for sure.
sentences.zh: 我们确实需要在NHS内部看到改变。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And with genetics and the way heritability works, how's your liver, Sharon?
sentences.zh: 关于遗传和遗传方式，莎伦，你的肝脏怎么样？

sentences.en: My liver so far is so good.
sentences.zh: 我的肝脏目前还不错。

sentences.en: So far, so good.
sentences.zh: 目前一切正常。

sentences.en: I had a liver scan done with the British Liver TruSt.
sentences.zh: 我参加了英国肝脏信托基金会的肝脏扫描。

sentences.en: They do something called the Love Your Liver Roadshow.
sentences.zh: 他们举办了一个叫“爱护你的肝脏”巡回宣传活动。

sentences.en: They're a charity, it's self-funded.
sentences.zh: 他们是一个慈善机构，资金是自筹的。

sentences.en: So I went along, had my liver checked.
sentences.zh: 所以我去检查了我的肝脏。

sentences.en: And the sonographer said to me, you know, your fatty range is fine.
sentences.zh: 超声波技师告诉我，你的脂肪含量在正常范围内。

sentences.en: Your liver stiffness is fine.
sentences.zh: 你的肝脏硬度也正常。

sentences.en: But, you know, because we know that your dad died from this, you cannot be too relaxed with your diet because your likelihood of getting it has, you know, is increased tenfold.
sentences.zh: 但因为我们知道你父亲死于这种病，你在饮食上绝不能掉以轻心，因为你患病的可能性增加了十倍。

sentences.en: So you need to make sure you're doing everything you can within reason to make sure that you don't develop this disease.
sentences.zh: 所以你需要确保在合理范围内尽一切努力，确保自己不会患上这种疾病。

sentences.en: And so sometimes I can become quite over-focused with my health and become quite anxious about, is this going to harm my liver?
sentences.zh: 所以有时我会对自己的健康过度关注，变得非常焦虑，担心这会不会伤害我的肝脏？

sentences.en: Am I okay to have this?
sentences.zh: 我吃这个没问题吧？

sentences.en: And I know that I shouldn't be doing that.
sentences.zh: 我知道我不该这样。

sentences.en: But it's just always at the back of my mind that, Sharon, you might develop this and you don't want your children to go through what you've been through, you know, with your dad.
sentences.zh: 但这总是在我脑海深处挥之不去，提醒我：莎伦，你可能会得这个病，你不想让你的孩子经历你和你爸爸经历过的那一切。

sentences.en: You don't want them to see that decline in somebody's health.
sentences.zh: 你不想让他们看到一个人健康状况的衰退。

sentences.en: And, you know, so I try and make a conscious effort to do whatever I can to support my liver health.
sentences.zh: 所以，我努力有意识地尽我所能去维护我的肝脏健康。

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: And actually, it is incredibly difficult to watch someone become very unwell, to become frail.
sentences.zh: 事实上，看着一个人变得非常虚弱、憔悴，确实非常痛苦。

sentences.en: It's distressing, you know, and someone that was previously very strong and capable to then not even be able to do things like stand up or wash or walk to the toilet.
sentences.zh: 这令人心碎，尤其是看到一个曾经非常强壮、能干的人，后来连站立、洗澡或走到厕所都做不到。

sentences.en: And you said that your dad had lost so much weight.
sentences.zh: 你说过你爸爸瘦了很多。

sentences.en: You gave us a really powerful example of that before we recorded.
sentences.zh: 在录制前，你给我们举了一个非常有力的例子。

sentences.en: Would you guide us through that?
sentences.zh: 能给我们讲讲吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So dad was in hospital.
sentences.zh: 当时爸爸在医院。

sentences.en: He'd just had his CTs drained and he was like, I can't find my watch.
sentences.zh: 他刚做完CT检查，然后他说，“我找不到我的手表了。”

sentences.en: We're like, dad, it's okay.
sentences.zh: 我们说，“爸爸，没关系。”

sentences.en: We'll find it.
sentences.zh: “我们会找到的。”

sentences.en: He said, no, no, I was wearing it.
sentences.zh: 他说，“不，不，我刚才还戴着它。”

sentences.en: I can't find it.
sentences.zh: “我找不到它了。”

sentences.en: And we were searching away and then he just, we could hear something.
sentences.zh: 我们正在四处寻找，然后我们听到了一些声音。

sentences.en: And his watch had basically gone from his wrist all the way up to his shoulder.
sentences.zh: 他的手表竟然从手腕滑到了肩膀上。

sentences.en: Now, this is a man who used to be very built to the point where his wrist and his watch used to be quite snug on his wriSt.
sentences.zh: 要知道，他以前是个非常壮实的人，他的手腕和手表之间曾经戴得很紧。

sentences.en: And that same watch was now on his shoulder.
sentences.zh: 而现在，同一块手表竟然滑到了他的肩膀上。

sentences.en: And that just shows how much muscle he had lost, how much weight he had loSt.
sentences.zh: 这足以说明他流失了多少肌肉，减轻了多少体重。

sentences.en: He'd become a former show of himself.
sentences.zh: 他已经变得形同枯槁。

sentences.en: When I think back to it, it's really heartbreaking.
sentences.zh: 每当回想起来，都让人心碎。

sentences.en: It's harrowing, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这太折磨人了，不是吗？

sentences.en: And when we're thinking about trauma work, that's one of the kind of bumps in the road that might keep kind of tripping you, tripping you up.
sentences.zh: 当我们谈论创伤处理时，这就是那种可能会让你不断绊倒的障碍之一。

sentences.en: And it stays with you, you know, you can't, I mean, yes, time, people say time heals.
sentences.zh: 它会一直伴随着你，你知道，人们常说时间能治愈一切。

sentences.en: It does in a way in terms of you get used to your new normal, but I will never, ever forget the pain he went through and what we've been through.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上确实如此，因为你会习惯新的生活常态，但我永远、永远不会忘记他所承受的痛苦，以及我们所经历的一切。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, thank you for talking to us about this and for sharing it.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你和我们谈论这些，也谢谢你的分享。

sentences.en: I know it's really challenging.
sentences.zh: 我知道这真的很不容易。

sentences.en: Do you talk to your children about their granddad?
sentences.zh: 你会和你的孩子们谈论她们的爷爷吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I tell them stories about their granddad, what he liked, what he didn't like.
sentences.zh: 会，我会给她们讲爷爷的故事，他喜欢什么，不喜欢什么。

sentences.en: You know, he was such a jolly character that I try and keep his memory alive.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他是个非常开朗的人，所以我努力让他的记忆鲜活下去。

sentences.en: And the girls know why I do what I do now, because my youngest one was like, you know, what is liver disease?
sentences.zh: 孩子们也知道我现在为什么做这些，因为我最小的孩子问我，“什么是肝病？”

sentences.en: Why do you talk about it so much?
sentences.zh: “你为什么总是谈论它？”

sentences.en: And I was like, well, you know, this is what took your granddad.
sentences.zh: 我说，这就是带走你们爷爷的病。

sentences.en: So if I can help one family out there to not go through what we've gone through, that's a huge win.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我能帮助一个家庭免于经历我们所经历的痛苦，那就是巨大的胜利。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And let's go right back to basics.
sentences.zh: 让我们回到最基础的问题。

sentences.en: Can you tell us where is our liver?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我们肝脏在哪里吗？

sentences.en: Where would we find that in our body?
sentences.zh: 我们在身体的哪个部位能找到它？

sentences.en: And if we were getting some liver gripe, I seem to remember when I've had hangovers in the past, that sort of dull ache on the back.
sentences.zh: 如果肝脏不舒服，我记得以前宿醉时，背部会有那种隐隐作痛的感觉。

sentences.en: Like, guide us through that.
